Figure 9.22 shows two typical solution curves. Regardless of the initial velocity, we see the body’s velocity tending toward the limiting value y = mg>k. This value, a stable equilibrium point, is called the body’s terminal velocity. Skydivers can vary their termi- nal velocity from 95 mph to 180 mph by changing the amount of body area opposing the fall, which affects the value of k.
